title: The SSF conformance PR added GET/PATCH/PUT stream handlers plus stream verify and status views without the add_stream provider permission check that the existing POST handler enforces, so any token holder for the app can read, modify, verify and disable its event streams.

vulnerable_findings.explanation: The viewset now includes DestroyModelMixin (and RetrieveModelMixin) with a queryset of `Stream.objects.all()` and no explicit ownership or permission checks. This allows any caller with access to the endpoint to delete or retrieve arbitrary Stream objects, constituting a missing authorization check (IDOR).

findings.explanation: The change only modifies a Django ORM filter call and adds a Python conditional. No raw SQL strings are constructed or concatenated with user‑controlled data, so there is no risk of SQL injection.

evidence.content:
class SSFStreamViewSet(
    mixins.RetrieveModelMixin,
    mixins.DestroyModelMixin,
    mixins.ListModelMixin,
    GenericViewSet,
):
    """SSFStream Viewset"""

    queryset = Stream.objects.all()

findings.suggested_fix: Add proper permission checks (e.g., IsAuthenticated & custom object‑level permission) and filter the queryset to only include streams owned by the requesting user or application. Restrict the DELETE operation to authorized users only.
